steps.body: A tally mark counts one. Every fifth mark crosses the four before it, bundling them into a five-group.
steps.narration: A tally mark counts one. Every fifth mark crosses the four before it, bundling them into a five-group.

widget.successFeedback: Cats shows one crossed five-group and two singles; Dogs shows four singles — the counts, drawn.

predict.prompt: You will tally 7 votes for Cats. What will the row look like?
predict.reveal: Every fifth mark crosses its group: 7 becomes one crossed five and two singles — 5, then 6, 7.

explanationVariants: Count fives inside 7: 1 crossed groups fit.

widget.prompt: 7 students voted. When you tally the votes in five-groups, how many CROSSED groups will there be?

commonErrors.feedback: That is the whole count of votes. Each crossed group bundles five of them; the question asks how many full bundles fit.
That is the number of leftover single marks after the five-groups, not the number of crossed groups.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Bundle the count into fives — each full bundle becomes one crossed group.

widget.prompt: 8 students voted. After the crossed five-groups, how many SINGLE marks will the tally show?

commonErrors.feedback: That is the number of crossed five-groups, not the leftover single marks.
That is the whole count. Only the marks left over after bundling fives stand alone.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Take out the full fives first — the marks that do not fill a five-group stand alone.

explanationVariants: 2 crossed five-groups make 10, plus 3 singles makes 13.
Read the tally backward: groups times five, plus the leftover singles.

widget.prompt: A tally row shows 2 crossed five-groups and 3 single marks. How many does it count?

commonErrors.feedback: That counts each crossed group as one mark, but a crossed group holds FIVE marks. Count the groups by fives, then add the singles.
That counts only the five-groups and skips the single marks after them. Count on from 10 by ones.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Each crossed group holds 5 — count the groups by fives, then add the leftover singles: 2 fives is 10, plus 3 is 13.

steps.body: How many more to the next group?
explanationVariants: A group needs 5; 3 singles are already there, so 5 − 3 = 2 more.
Count up from 3 to 5: 2 more marks complete the group.

widget.prompt: 13 students voted. The tally shows 2 crossed five-groups and 3 single marks. How many MORE votes are needed to cross a THIRD group?

commonErrors.feedback: 3 is how many singles are already there. The question asks how many MORE are needed to reach 5: 5 − 3 = 2.
8 would start a whole new group without using the 3 marks already there. Only 5 − 3 = 2 more marks are needed to finish this group.

widget.fallbackFeedback: A group needs 5 marks. 3 are already there, so 5 − 3 = 2 more are needed.
